rv.q: Everything comes together with such skill in "Kiss of the Spider Woman," at the Broadhurst Theater, that the musical outdazzles every other song-and-dance extravaganza on Broadway.
The best new musical of 1993 — and for the last few seasons of drought — has to be Kiss of the Spider Woman.

But what’s a star-making performance when the package surrounding the actor is otherwise so ordinary and un-cosmic? Lopez, while impressive as a vamping, dreamed-up screen star in the silhouette of Rita Hayworth or any other pin-up you’d too have plastered on the walls of your prison cell if you were a gay Hollywood-movie obsessive, doesn’t get ...
It’s disappointing that what they are peddling has become so distorted.
Lopez still insists on singing. Her voice sounds fine on heavily produced dance tracks, but there is no obscuring its thinness here.
